questions.q: A fitted simple linear regression model is \( \hat{y} = 7x + 18 \). What is the predicted target value \( \hat{y} \) when the input feature is \( x = 4 \)?
questions.answer: Substitute \( x = 4 \) into the regression equation: \( \hat{y} = 7(4) + 18 = 28 + 18 = 46 \).

questions.q: In a multiple linear regression model, the Sum of Squared Errors is \( \text{SSE} = 20 \) and the Total Sum of Squares is \( \text{SST} = 100 \). What is the coefficient of determination \( R^2 \)?
questions.answer: The coefficient of determination measures the proportion of variance explained: \( R^2 = 1 - \frac{\text{SSE}}{\text{SST}} = 1 - \frac{20}{100} = 1 - 0.20 = 0.80 \).

questions.q: For a bivariate feature dataset, \( \text{Cov}(x, y) = 12 \), \( \text{Var}(x) = 4 \), \( \bar{x} = 5 \), and \( \bar{y} = 25 \). Compute the OLS regression slope \( \hat{\beta}_1 \) and intercept \( \hat{\beta}_0 \).
questions.answer: The OLS slope is \( \hat{\beta}_1 = \frac{\text{Cov}(x, y)}{\text{Var}(x)} = \frac{12}{4} = 3 \). The intercept is \( \hat{\beta}_0 = \bar{y} - \hat{\beta}_1\bar{x} = 25 - (3)(5) = 25 - 15 = 10 \).

questions.q: Consider a dataset of \( n \) observations \( (x_i, y_i) \) for \( i = 1, \dots, n \), where \( x_i \) are scalar predictor variables and \( y_i \) are scalar response variables. The ordinary least squares (OLS) estimates for the intercept \( \beta_0 \) and the slope \( \beta_1 \) of the linear model \( y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x + \epsilon \) are given by \( \hat{\beta}_1 = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \bar{x})(y_i - \bar{y})}{\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \bar{x})^2} \) and \( \hat{\beta}_0 = \bar{y} - \hat{\beta}_1 \bar{x} \). Suppose we have a dataset where \( n = 5 \), \( \sum x_i = 15 \), \( \sum y_i = 30 \), \( \sum x_i^2 = 55 \), \( \sum y_i^2 = 210 \), and \( \sum x_i y_i = 105 \). A new data point \( (x_6, y_6) \) is added to the dataset. If the new regression line that minimizes the sum of squared errors for the \( n+1 = 6 \) points is parallel to the original regression line (i.e., \( \hat{\beta}_1^{\text{new}} = \hat{\beta}_1^{\text{old}} \)), what is the value of \( y_6 \) in terms of \( x_6 \)?
questions.answer: For the original \( n = 5 \) observations, \( \bar{x} = \frac{15}{5} = 3 \) and \( \bar{y} = \frac{30}{5} = 6 \). The sums of squares are \( S_{xx} = 55 - 5(3^2) = 10 \) and \( S_{xy} = 105 - 5(3)(6) = 15 \), giving slope \( \hat{\beta}_1 = \frac{15}{10} = 1.5 \) and intercept \( \hat{\beta}_0 = 6 - 1.5(3) = 1.5 \). When a 6th point \( (x_6, y_6) \) lying on the existing regression line \( y_6 = 1.5x_6 + 1.5 \) is added, the residual is zero and the OLS slope remains unchanged at \( 1.5 \).

questions.q: An Ordinary Least Squares regression model (#1) achieves residual sum of squares \(\text{SSE} = 5\) on data with total sum of squares \(\text{SST} = 20\). Compute the coefficient of determination \(R^2\).
questions.answer: By definition, \(R^2 = 1 - \frac{\text{SSE}}{\text{SST}} = 1 - \frac{5}{20} = \frac{3}{4}\).

questions.q: In dataset #2, sample variance is \(s_x^2 = 3\), sample covariance is \(s_{xy} = -8\), \(\bar{x} = 3\), and \(\bar{y} = 10\). Find the OLS slope \(\hat{\beta}_1\).
questions.answer: The univariate OLS slope estimator is \(\hat{\beta}_1 = \frac{s_{xy}}{s_x^2} = \frac{-8}{3} = -\frac{8}{3}\).
